title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 59–61). M = M̄_{g,ν} (presumably the Deligne–Mumford stack) carries its boundary stratification by the number of nodes d. In the notation of these notes:
- D_d is the normalised d-fold self-intersection of the boundary divisor, i.e. curves together with a choice of d (unordered) nodes. D_0 = M̄ and D_1 is the normalisation of the boundary divisor.
- D_d^! → D_d is the S_d-Galois étale cover that orders the d nodes.
- T_d is the rank-d local system Z^{chosen nodes}; its pullback T_d^! to D_d^! is trivial, equal to Z^d with S_d permuting the factors.
- On D_d^! one has the maps s_i : D_d^! → D_1 picking out the i-th node, and the line bundles L_{d,i} = s_i^* L_1, where L_1 is the normal sheaf of the local immersion D_1 → D_0. Let L*_{d,i} be the associated G_m-torsors (punctured line bundles), and set P_d^! = ∏_i L*_{d,i}, a G_m^d-torsor.

This page.
- (190) Define the split torus G_d^! = G_m ⊗_Z T_d^! ≅ G_m^d, with S_d acting by permuting factors.
- Galois descent along D_d^! → D_d gives the twisted torus G_d = G_m ⊗ T_d on D_d. Since S_d acts compatibly on P_d^!, this also gives (191) a G_d-torsor P_d on D_d.
- The fibres of P_d are torsors under a rank-d torus, so H_1 = π_1 of a fibre is the cocharacter lattice. Hence (192) T_d ≅ the local system of H_1 (or π_1) of the fibres of P_d. Topologically, T_d is the lattice generated by the Dehn twists around the d vanishing cycles.
- P_d is the algebraic model of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum. Its fundamental groupoid ΠP_d is the object of interest.
- One restricts to the open part D_d^* = D_d minus the images of D_{d',d} → D_d for d' > d, i.e. curves with exactly d nodes. With P_d^* := P_d|D_d^*, one takes ΠP_d^*, the groupoid used 'for the rest'.

Programme announced. Study how T_d, G_d, P_d, P_d^*, T_d^!, G_d^!, P_d^!, ΠP_d and ΠP_d^* vary with d. For d ≥ d' ≥ 0 there is a correspondence D_d ← D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}: an étale cover (choose d' of the d nodes) followed by a local immersion (partial smoothing). On the next page this yields the 'tautological' surjection T_d → T_{d'}, which is the coordinate projection Z^d → Z^{d'}.

Purpose. Build a combinatorial and algebraic model of the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: the tower of fundamental groupoids of punctured tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary strata, with their face and degeneracy-like transition maps. This feeds the Teichmüller-tower programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Minor: D_1 → D_0 is only a local (unramified) immersion of the normalised boundary, not a global regular immersion. 'Normal sheaf' must therefore be taken along s_i, which is what the construction implicitly does. Everything is fine at the level of stacks.
Minor: the margin hesitates between 'normal' and 'conormal' for L_1. This only changes the sign convention (orientation) of the identification of T_d with H_1 of the fibres.
Minor gap: P_d^* only models the punctured tubular neighbourhood up to homotopy, and only over the open stratum. Grothendieck evidently knows this, hence the restriction to D_d^*.
Notation: the bottom line writes D_{d*}, which should be D_d.

ideas.what: Twisted torus G_d = G_m ⊗ T_d over the d-node stratum, obtained by descent from G_m^d with S_d permuting factors
ideas.modern_name: Torus attached to the local system of nodes; the log-structure / monodromy torus of a boundary stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford (1969) and in log geometry (F. Kato, K. Kato, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the structure at infinity only qualitatively

ideas.what: Torsor P_d = product of punctured normal bundles of the boundary branches, as an algebraic model of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of a stratum
ideas.modern_name: Punctured normal bundle / Kato–Nakayama-type torus bundle over a boundary stratum; tangential base points

ideas.what: T_d ≅ H_1 = π_1 of the torus fibres of P_d, i.e. the free abelian group of Dehn twists along the vanishing cycles
ideas.modern_name: Local monodromy lattice / Dehn-twist subgroup at a boundary point

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoids ΠP_d and ΠP_d^* over open strata, and their variation with d via the correspondences D_d ← D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid at infinity / stratified (exit-path-like) structure of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}; Teichmüller tower with boundary groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Boggi (fundamental groups at infinity)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the idea

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds an algebraic G_m-torsor model of the deleted neighbourhoods of all boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}, organised functorially in d through the correspondences D_d ← D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}. This is essentially an algebraic version of the Kato–Nakayama / log-structure description of the boundary, used here to define a system of fundamental groupoids at infinity. He made this explicit well before log geometry was applied to M̄_g, but it is not a new result.
missed.quote: et par descente on trouve sur D_d un torseur (191) P_d torseur sur D_d, de groupe G_d ... (192) T_d ≃ syst. local des H_1 (ou des π_1) des fibres de P_d
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest: it shows the boundary-groupoid ('structure à l'infini') programme was worked out concretely by Grothendieck, anticipating Ihara–Nakamura and Boggi-type constructions. Mathematically it is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but now-standard construction: twisted torus, punctured normal bundles and Dehn-twist lattice over the boundary strata. It is an interesting unpublished detail of Grothendieck's own set-up for the structure at infinity, but there is no result absent from the later literature.

'et par suite ... [?]' probably reads 'et par suite on a canoniquement' or 'et par suite on a'.
'plus essentiellement nous pour la suite' likely reads 'plus essentiellement pour nous pour la suite'.
The insertion before D_d^* reads 'l'ouvert'. The crossed-out word appears to be 'le groupoïde', with something like 'Géométrie'/'grossier' scribbled above it.
Above 'Considérons dans' the insertion appears to be 'un couple' or 'un exemple'. The struck-out 'd≥d'' is rewritten as 'd ≥ d' ≥ 0'.
